title: Tras: indicar lo que viene después

sections.content: Tras (after) is a compact, more formal alternative to después de, common in historical writing. It can be followed by a noun (tras el bombardeo) or an infinitive when the same subject performs both actions (tras hacerse con el poder). These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: Tras el bombardeo del palacio presidencial, Allende murió ese mismo día dentro del edificio.
items.english: After the bombing of the presidential palace, Allende died that same day inside the building.

items.spanish: Tras hacerse con el poder, Pinochet estableció una junta militar que gobernaría Chile durante diecisiete años.
items.english: After seizing power, Pinochet established a military junta that would govern Chile for seventeen years.

items.spanish: Tras un periodo inicial de mucha inestabilidad económica, el régimen entregó el manejo de la economía a los "Chicago Boys".
items.english: After an initial period of considerable economic instability, the regime handed over the management of the economy to the "Chicago Boys".

items.spanish: Tras el fin de la dictadura, los gobiernos democráticos chilenos posteriores mantendrían en gran medida este mismo modelo económico.
items.english: After the end of the dictatorship, later Chilean democratic governments would largely maintain this same economic model.

sections.content: Tras + infinitive requires the same subject in both clauses, just like después de + infinitive -- tras hacerse con el poder, Pinochet estableció... means Pinochet did both the seizing and the establishing.
